Subject: Compute profile evaluation for Crestline dedicated commit — H100 / A100 / L4 tradeoffs

Jordan / Procurement team —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Attached is a short compute-profile workbook (crestline_compute_profiles_v1.xlsx) and a one-page hedged capacity plan (hedged_capacity_plan_v1.pdf) that map Crestline's stated workload patterns to a recommended Dedicated pool mix. High level summary first, then a few clarifying asks so we can lock in expected capacity and price.

Executive summary (TL;DR)
- Recommendation: Hybrid pool across A100 (primary), a small H100 pool for long-context / low-latency tails, and L4 nodes for high-volume embedding/cheap-inference paths.
- Why hybrid: A100 provides the best cost-performance for most of your models (mixed precision, decent memory for 8k-16k contexts). H100 is beneficial for sustained 32k/64k context runs and p95 latency-sensitive user flows. L4 is by far the cheapest for embedding/semantic-similarity workloads and batched offline inference.
- Hedging: We propose an initial allocation of ~60% A100, 25% L4, 15% H100 (by GPU-count), with automated routing and fallback policies. Plan includes 30% burstable buffer for traffic spikes.

Key tradeoffs to confirm
- Typical prompt+history length (tokens) per request and % of requests that require long context (>=32k).
- Concurrency targets (steady-state QPS and expected p95 latency SLO).
- Expected embedding throughput (qps and batch window for offline jobs).
- Do you require isolated memory (no shared tenancy) for certain channels (PII/regulatory)?

Questions for you (short answers appreciated)
- Avg tokens in prompt + response: ?
- % of requests that need 32k context: ?
- Steady concurrency target (concurrent streams or QPS): ?
- Business preference: strict p95 latency (<250ms) vs unit cost sensitivity?

Next steps: if these align with your expectations we can produce a formal reserved capacity quote and start a 4-week provisioning timeline from signature. I looped Ben (pricing) and Dev (inference infra) for details.

Attachments: crestline_compute_profiles_v1.xlsx (workbook), hedged_capacity_plan_v1.pdf (one-pager)

Sofia —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the workbook. A few quick answers below to help ground your recommendations:
- Avg tokens (prompt + response): ~1,200 tokens for conversational flows; however ~8% of calls are analytics queries that push to 28k-32k context.
- Embedding workload: heavy — approx 150k embedding requests/day, mostly batched (window ~5–10s) from our batch pipeline.
- Concurrency: steady-state 160 concurrent streams (peaks to ~320 for launches).
- p95 latency target: 300ms for live chat, embeddings can be relaxed to 1–2s.
- Regulatory: search personalization channel needs strong isolation (PII), other channels can be multi-tenant on dedicated but shared pools are fine.

Also: curious how caching (prefix / KV) impacts the SKU split — would a larger L4 pool help if we can cache hot prefixes?

If you can, include a notional cost delta for the hedged plan vs an A100-only approach — we need to present both to procurement.

Jordan / team —

Appreciate the specifics — those numbers help. Quick technical breakdown and a proposed notional capacity mapping you can use in procurement slides. I'm keeping this high level (we can share the workbook numbers) and adding caching/tiling context.

Assumptions (for notional sizing)
- Model footprints (approx memory working set, KV included):
  - Long-context model (32k): ~70–80 GB working set on GPU (with KV & activations); best served on H100-80GB-class instances.
  - Standard generation model (8k–16k typical): ~30–50 GB working set; A100-40/80GB variants handle these with good throughput.
  - Embedding model (smaller): ~6–12 GB working set; L4 (24GB) or lighter A2-style instances are very cost-effective for batched throughput.

How caching helps
- Prefix/KV cache reduces per-request working set for repeatable conversational flows. If you have strong cache locality (hot sessions), effective concurrency demand on large-memory GPUs drops; you can push a larger portion of traffic to A100 or even L4 for some off-path requests.
- For the 8% long-context cases, caching helps less — these are cold large-context windows, so H100 memory remains important.

Notional capacity mapping (GPU counts are illustrative for your concurrency targets)
- Baseline steady: 24 x A100 (primary for 70% of traffic), 6 x H100 (reserved for 32k / p95-sensitive tails), 10 x L4 (embedding & cheap-batch paths).
- Bursting buffer: additional 8 GPUs that can be tiled between A100/L4 during peaks.
- Routing policy: auto-route long-context reqs to H100; high-priority live chat pinned to pool with p95 SLO; embeddings routed to L4 via bulk batch queues.

Cost delta (very rough, ballpark)
- A100-only (to meet p95 and 32k tails via scale-up): ~+18% unit cost vs hedged plan due to inefficient memory headroom and larger headroom multiplier.
- Hedged hybrid plan (A100 + small H100 + L4): better unit $/token for embeddings and most gen traffic, while keeping p95 tail on H100.

Operational notes
- We recommend autoscaling thresholds that respect model warm-up and KV priming times (e.g., micro-burst tolerance with prefix cached warmups).
- For the personalized search channel (PII), use dedicated A100 or H100 slice (no cross-tenant sharing).

If this looks right, Ben can draft the price delta table and Sofia can schedule a short ops walk-through to confirm provisioning lead times.

—Dev

Jordan / Procurement team —

Following up with a concise recommendation and next steps so procurement has something clean to review. Based on your traffic profile (160 steady / peaks 320, 8% long-context, heavy embeddings) we recommend the hedged hybrid plan. Highlights below:

Final recommended hedge (proposal)
- Initial committed pool (GPU counts): 20 x A100, 6 x H100, 12 x L4.
- Burstable capacity: 8 GPUs as dynamic buffer (auto-swap between pool types).
- Isolation: dedicate 2 x A100 or H100 GPUs to the personalization channel to satisfy PII isolation.
- Routing & SLOs: route >=32k requests to H100; enforce 300ms p95 for live chat on pinned pool; embeddings go to L4 batch queues (1–2s SLO).

Procurement-ready artifacts (attached + links):
- hedged_capacity_plan_v1.pdf (summary + provisioning timeline)
- crestline_compute_profiles_v1.xlsx (detailed assumptions & GPU math)
- HubSpot deal: https://hubspot.example/deal/CR-4729 (Ben will add price table)
- Provisioning lead time: 4 weeks from signature for baseline pool; 6 weeks if H100 ordering lead times apply in your region.

Ask: please confirm by EOD Thu whether we should:
A) Proceed to a formal reserved capacity quote with the above hedged counts, or
B) Run a short A/B comparison quote for A100-only vs Hedged hybrid (Ben will include line-item deltas).

If you confirm (A) we'll kick off DocuSign and timeline planning; if (B) Ben will send a 48-hour comparative pricing doc.

Thanks — happy to hop on a 30m call if that helps speed things up.

Best,
